Build a missing_taxa_list from taxonomic tables

Source: R/build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy.R
build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy.Rd

Build a ready-to-be-used missing_taxa_list object based on taxonomic information from the backbone phylogeny and the taxa to graft. The missing_taxa_list can then be used as input for phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades().

Target clades, sister clades and excluded subclades are identified with taxonomic names (e.g., "Homo") or with taxonomic levels (e.g., "Genus") instead of tips or node IDs. The function retrieves the MRCA node of each taxonomic group in the backbone phylogeny, checks that the group is monophyletic, and writes each clade as a pair of tips, as expected by phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list().

Taxonomic tables are the go-to option for large phylogenies with neatly defined taxonomic levels (see 'When to use taxonomic tables' in Details). Use phylograftR::import_taxonomic_table() to read the tables directly from files.

For a finer level of control on the clades to use as target clades, sister clades, and/or excluded subclades, you can use alternative functions that define those clades based on any node IDs or pairs of tips used to identify MRCA: see phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list() and phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list().

Usage

build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy(
  backbone_taxonomic_table,
  missing_taxa_taxonomic_table,
  phy,
  non_monophyletic = c("exclude", "mrca", "error"),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

backbone_taxonomic_table

Data frame. Taxonomy of the tips of the backbone phylogeny, with one row per tip. The first column must be named Taxa and holds the tip labels of phy. All the other columns are taxonomic levels (e.g., Family, Subfamily, Tribe, Genus, but they can be anything), usually from the broadest to the narrowest. The values of a level are the names of the taxonomic groups (e.g., "Homo"). Levels do not have to be informed for all the tips: blank cells and NA are missing values. See Details for the constraints on the names of the levels and groups.

missing_taxa_taxonomic_table

Data frame. Description of the taxa to graft, with one row per taxon. Columns Taxa (names of the taxa to graft) and Type ("taxa" or "clades") are required, as well as the column of the clade to use for grafting (Target_clade or Sister_clade). Entries can be either the name of the taxonomic group (e.g., "Homo") or the taxonomic level of the taxa to use (e.g., Genus). Next columns provide the taxonomic levels of the taxa to graft using the same names as in backbone_taxonomic_table (e.g., Family, Subfamily, Tribe, Genus, but they can be anything). Other optional columns provide additional information on constraints to use for grafting: Excluded_subclades, include_target_clade_stem, exclude_subclades_stem, and allowed_states, as defined in missing_taxa_list argument of the grafting functions (phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()). See 'Missing taxa taxonomic table' in Details section for an extended description.

phy

An object of class "phylo". The backbone phylogeny on which the taxa will be grafted.

non_monophyletic

Character string. What to do when a taxonomic group is not monophyletic in phy, i.e., when the clade defined by the MRCA of its tips also holds tips of other groups of the same level. Must be one of "exclude" (default), "mrca" or "error". See 'Non-monophyletic groups' in Details.

verbose

Logical. Whether to print a summary of the conversion. Default is TRUE.

Value

A missing_taxa_list object as returned by phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list(): a list ready-to-be-used as input of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() if all the taxa have Type = "taxa", or of phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() if they all have Type = "clades". If both types are present, a list with two elements, taxa and clades, each holding the missing_taxa_list of one type.

The attribute "taxonomic_groups" is a data frame with one row per taxonomic group used, with the columns Group, Level, n_members (number of tips of the group), clade_node (MRCA node ID in phy), clade_tips (pair of tips defining the clade), n_tips_clade (number of tips of the clade), n_foreign (tips of other groups in the clade), n_unannotated (tips without value at this level in the clade), and monophyletic.

Details

When to use taxonomic tables

Taxonomic tables are the go-to option for large phylogenies with neatly defined taxonomic levels (e.g., Family, Subfamily, Tribe, Genus). The taxonomy of the backbone is provided once, and each taxon to graft only needs its own taxonomic levels: the constraints (target clade, sister clade, excluded subclades) are written with the names of the groups or of the taxonomic levels to use, and the clades are retrieved from the phylogeny. The same group is therefore always the same clade, whatever the number of taxa, which avoids the typos and inconsistencies of clades written taxon by taxon, and the tables can be taken as such from a taxonomic database.

The limit is that only the taxonomic groups of the backbone table can be used as clades. To fine-tune the grafting of some taxa with any other node of the phylogeny (e.g., a clade without a name, a part of a group, or a group of several genera), define their clades by tips or node IDs with phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list() or phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() (see 'Fine-tuning the clades' in their Details sections).

Both routes return the same missing_taxa_list, so a list built from taxonomic tables can be adjusted afterwards.

Backbone taxonomic table

Names of taxonomic levels (the column names; e.g., "Genus") and names of taxonomic groups (their values; e.g., "Homo") must be unambiguous:

  • A level name cannot be the name of a tip, of a taxon to graft, or of a group.

  • A group name belongs to a single level: the same name cannot be found in two columns (e.g., a Family cannot be named the same as a Genus).

  • Level names and group names cannot contain ";". Level names cannot be "Taxa", "Type" or the names of the other columns of missing_taxa_taxonomic_table.

  • All the tips of backbone_taxonomic_table must be in phy. Tips of phy absent from the table are allowed (with a warning).

Missing taxa taxonomic table

  • Taxa (Required): Names of the taxa to graft. Names must be unique and absent from phy$tip.label.

  • Type (Required): "taxa" for taxa grafted with phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() within a target clade, or "clades" for taxa grafted with phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() as a sister of a clade.

  • Taxonomic levels (Optional): Same columns as in backbone_taxonomic_table. They are used to retrieve the taxonomic group of the taxon when Target_clade, Sister_clade, and/or Excluded_subclades (see below) use a taxonomic level (e.g., "Genus") rather than directly a taxonomic group (e.g., "Homo") as identification. Columns that are not levels of the backbone, nor one of the columns listed here, are ignored with a warning.

  • Target_clade (Required for Type = "taxa") or Sister_clade (Required for Type = "clades"): A single taxonomic group, written either as the name of the group (e.g., "Homo"), or as the name of a taxonomic level (e.g., "Genus"). If a taxonomic level is provided, the group will be identified as recorded in the column of the same name in missing_taxa_taxonomic_table (e.g., "Genus" with Genus = "Camponotus" gives the clade of the genus Camponotus). It is an error if the group is absent from the backbone, or if the taxon has no value at the requested level.

  • Excluded_subclades (Optional, Type = "taxa"): Subclades of the target clade where the taxon is known not to belong, separated by semicolons (e.g., "Pheidole; Camponotus"). Each one is a group or a level name, as in Target_clade.

  • $include_target_clade_stem (Optional, Type = "taxa"): Logical. Whether the stem branch of the target clade is a valid placement to graft this taxa (NA uses the global argument set in the grafting function).

  • $exclude_subclades_stem (Optional, Type = "taxa"): Logical. Whether the stem branch of the excluded clade(s) is/are a excluded from grafting too. Separated by semicolons if multiple Excluded_subclades are provided (NA uses the global argument set in the grafting function).

  • $allowed_states (Optional): For each taxon, the states of a simmap in which it can be grafted (see the simmap argument of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() or phylograftR::graft_missing_clades()), separated by commas. If multiple traits are used, each set of states must be separated by semicolons (e.g., "blue, red; low"). It is accepted with both Target_clade and Sister_clade. (NA uses the global argument set in the grafting function).

Non-monophyletic groups

What to do when a taxonomic group is not monophyletic in phy, i.e., when the clade defined by the MRCA of its tips also holds tips of other groups of the same level?

  • non_monophyletic = "exclude" (default): For target clades, intruders (i.e., tips from other groups descending from the MRCA) are added to the Excluded_subclades of the taxon (with their stem, exclude_subclades_stem = TRUE), so the taxon is never grafted among intruders. Intruders nested within an excluded subclade provided by the user are not added. Intruders cannot be removed from a sister clade or from a group of Excluded_subclades: the clade of the MRCA is used with a warning (as for "mrca"). For Excluded_subclades, all the branches descending from the MRCA are then excluded, including the ones of intruders.

  • non_monophyletic = "mrca": The clade of the MRCA is used as such, with a warning, including its intruders.

  • non_monophyletic = "error": Stop if one group used is not monophyletic.

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::import_taxonomic_table() to read the taxonomic tables from external files.

  • phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() to read a table of missing taxa from a file, with clades defined by tips or node IDs.

  • phylograftR::build_missing_taxa_list() to build a missing_taxa_list from a data.frame loaded in R, with clades defined by tips or node IDs.

  • phylograftR::build_total_richness_per_clades() and phylograftR::import_total_richness_per_clades() to prepare total_richness_per_clades for the unsampled species.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa based on target clades and excluded subclades using the list.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() to graft groups of missing taxa as sister clades using the list.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa_and_clades() to graft missing taxa and missing clades in one run, with a single set of inputs.

Author

Maël Doré

Examples

## Load the toy backbone phylogeny and its taxonomy
data(toy_backbone)
data(toy_backbone_taxonomic_table)
head(toy_backbone_taxonomic_table)
#>   Taxa   Family Subfamily     Tribe Genus
#> 1  t26 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>
#> 2   t2 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>
#> 3  t21 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>
#> 4  t16 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>
#> 5  t11 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>
#> 6   t4 Family_A Subfam_A2 Tribe_A2a  <NA>

## Load the taxonomic table of the taxa to graft
data(toy_missing_taxa_taxonomic_table)
toy_missing_taxa_taxonomic_table
#>           Taxa   Type   Family Subfamily     Tribe   Genus Target_clade
#> 1      New_sp1   taxa Family_A      <NA>      <NA>    <NA>       Family
#> 2      New_sp2   taxa Family_A      <NA>      <NA>    <NA>       Family
#> 3      New_sp3   taxa Family_A      <NA>      <NA>    <NA>       Family
#> 4      New_sp4   taxa Family_B      <NA>      <NA>    <NA>     Family_B
#> 5      New_sp5   taxa Family_B Subfam_B1      <NA>    <NA>    Subfamily
#> 6      New_sp6   taxa Family_B Subfam_B2  Tribe_B2    <NA>        Gen_2
#> 7      New_sp7   taxa Family_B Subfam_B2  Tribe_B2    <NA>        Tribe
#> 8  Genus_a_sp1 clades Family_B Subfam_B1      <NA> Genus_a         <NA>
#> 9  Genus_a_sp2 clades Family_B Subfam_B1      <NA> Genus_a         <NA>
#> 10 Genus_b_sp1 clades Family_A Subfam_A1 Tribe_A1b Genus_b         <NA>
#>    Sister_clade  Excluded_subclades include_target_clade_stem
#> 1          <NA> Subfam_A1;Tribe_A2a                      TRUE
#> 2          <NA>     Tribe_A2a;Gen_3                      TRUE
#> 3          <NA>                <NA>                     FALSE
#> 4          <NA>                <NA>                        NA
#> 5          <NA>               Gen_1                      TRUE
#> 6          <NA>                <NA>                        NA
#> 7          <NA>                <NA>                     FALSE
#> 8         Gen_1                <NA>                        NA
#> 9         Gen_1                <NA>                        NA
#> 10        Tribe                <NA>                        NA
#>    exclude_subclades_stem
#> 1              TRUE;FALSE
#> 2              FALSE;TRUE
#> 3                    <NA>
#> 4                    <NA>
#> 5                    <NA>
#> 6                    <NA>
#> 7                    <NA>
#> 8                    <NA>
#> 9                    <NA>
#> 10                   <NA>

# The taxa to graft with graft_missing_taxa() (Type = "taxa") use different types of constraints:
# * New_sp1: grafted in its family (Target_clade = "Family" is the family of the taxon,
#   i.e., "Family_A"), but not in the subfamily "Subfam_A1" nor in the tribe "Tribe_A2a"
#   (Excluded_subclades).
#   The stem of the family is available (include_target_clade_stem),
#   the stem of "Subfam_A1" is excluded too,
#   but not the one of "Tribe_A2a" (exclude_subclades_stem).
# * New_sp2: same target clade, but excluded subclades are a tribe
#   and a genus with a single species ("Gen_3"), and the stem is excluded for the genus only.
# * New_sp3: same target clade, without excluded subclades and
#   without access to the stem of the family.
# * New_sp4: grafted in the family "Family_B", written directly with the name of the group.
# * New_sp5: grafted in its subfamily (Target_clade = "Subfamily", i.e., "Subfam_B1"),
#   except in the genus "Gen_1".
# * New_sp6: grafted on the terminal branch of the only species
#   of the genus "Gen_2" (a single tip).
# * New_sp7: grafted in its tribe (Target_clade = "Tribe", i.e., "Tribe_B2"),
#   without access to the stem.

# The taxa to graft with graft_missing_clades() (Type = "clades") use sister clades:
# * Genus_a_sp1 and Genus_a_sp2: belong to a new genus, and have the same sister clade ("Gen_1"),
#   so they are grafted together as a missing clade.
# * Genus_b_sp1: grafted as the sister of its own tribe (Sister_clade = "Tribe", i.e., "Tribe_A1b").

## Build the missing taxa lists associated to these taxonomic tables
missing_taxa_lists <- build_missing_taxa_list_from_taxonomy(
  backbone_taxonomic_table = toy_backbone_taxonomic_table,
  missing_taxa_taxonomic_table = toy_missing_taxa_taxonomic_table,
  phy = toy_backbone)
#> 7 taxa for graft_missing_taxa() and 3 for graft_missing_clades() built from 10 taxonomic group(s), 0 not monophyletic. See attr(, "taxonomic_groups").

# Since both types of taxa to graft were provided,
# the output contains one list per grafting function
names(missing_taxa_lists)
#> [1] "taxa"   "clades"
str(missing_taxa_lists$taxa, max.level = 1) # Missing_taxa_list for graft_missing_taxa()
#> List of 6
#>  $ Taxon_name               : chr [1:7] "New_sp1" "New_sp2" "New_sp3" "New_sp4" ...
#>  $ Target_clade             :List of 7
#>  $ Target_clade_name        : Named chr [1:7] "Family_A" "Family_A" "Family_A" "Family_B" ...
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:7] "New_sp1" "New_sp2" "New_sp3" "New_sp4" ...
#>  $ include_target_clade_stem: Named logi [1:7] TRUE TRUE FALSE NA TRUE NA ...
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:7] "New_sp1" "New_sp2" "New_sp3" "New_sp4" ...
#>  $ Excluded_subclades       :List of 7
#>  $ exclude_subclades_stem   :List of 7
str(missing_taxa_lists$clades, max.level = 1) # Missing_taxa_list for graft_missing_clades()
#> List of 3
#>  $ Taxon_name       : chr [1:3] "Genus_a_sp1" "Genus_a_sp2" "Genus_b_sp1"
#>  $ Sister_clade     :List of 3
#>  $ Sister_clade_name: Named chr [1:3] "Gen_1" "Gen_1" "Tribe_A1b"
#>   ..- attr(*, "names")= chr [1:3] "Genus_a_sp1" "Genus_a_sp2" "Genus_b_sp1"

# Clades are written as pairs of tips, and named after their taxonomic groups
missing_taxa_lists$taxa$Target_clade
#> $New_sp1
#> [1] "t26" "t19"
#> 
#> $New_sp2
#> [1] "t26" "t19"
#> 
#> $New_sp3
#> [1] "t26" "t19"
#> 
#> $New_sp4
#> [1] "t8"  "t22"
#> 
#> $New_sp5
#> [1] "t8" "t7"
#> 
#> $New_sp6
#> [1] "t5"
#> 
#> $New_sp7
#> [1] "t5"  "t12"
#> 
missing_taxa_lists$taxa$Excluded_subclades$New_sp1
#> $Subfam_A1
#> [1] "t10" "t19"
#> 
#> $Tribe_A2a
#> [1] "t26" "t4" 
#> 
missing_taxa_lists$taxa$exclude_subclades_stem$New_sp1
#> Subfam_A1 Tribe_A2a 
#>      TRUE     FALSE 
missing_taxa_lists$clades$Sister_clade
#> $Genus_a_sp1
#> [1] "t13" "t27"
#> 
#> $Genus_a_sp2
#> [1] "t13" "t27"
#> 
#> $Genus_b_sp1
#> [1] "t18" "t19"
#> 

# The taxa to graft as clades share their sister clade, so they will be grafted together
missing_taxa_lists$clades$Sister_clade_name
#> Genus_a_sp1 Genus_a_sp2 Genus_b_sp1 
#>     "Gen_1"     "Gen_1" "Tribe_A1b" 

# Information on the groups used
attr(missing_taxa_lists, "taxonomic_groups")
#>        Group     Level n_members clade_node clade_tips n_tips_clade n_foreign
#> 1   Family_A    Family        17         32    t26,t19           17         0
#> 2   Family_B    Family        13         33     t8,t22           13         0
#> 3  Subfam_B1 Subfamily         9         34      t8,t7            9         0
#> 4      Gen_2     Genus         1         27         t5            1         0
#> 5   Tribe_B2     Tribe         3         53     t5,t12            3         0
#> 6      Gen_1     Genus         3         50    t13,t27            3         0
#> 7  Tribe_A1b     Tribe         2         40    t18,t19            2         0
#> 8  Subfam_A1 Subfamily         8         37    t10,t19            8         0
#> 9  Tribe_A2a     Tribe         6         39     t26,t4            6         0
#> 10     Gen_3     Genus         1         14        t30            1         0
#>    n_unannotated monophyletic
#> 1              0         TRUE
#> 2              0         TRUE
#> 3              0         TRUE
#> 4              0         TRUE
#> 5              0         TRUE
#> 6              0         TRUE
#> 7              0         TRUE
#> 8              0         TRUE
#> 9              0         TRUE
#> 10             0         TRUE

# The lists can be used for grafting
grafted_taxa <- graft_missing_taxa(toy_backbone, missing_taxa_lists$taxa, verbose = FALSE)
grafted_clades <- graft_missing_clades(toy_backbone, missing_taxa_lists$clades, verbose = FALSE)
